answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to grow a reputation garden over time: newcomers may only take small, escrowed jobs, and payment is released only after the counterparty verifies the work. Like a ripple spreading across an ocean, one fake identity cannot fake months of verified completions, and thousands of fresh identities hold no history. Attackers must fund and operate every fake for months, paying escrow and fees, while honest agents accumulate trust that decays if idle, making mass fakery costlier than the fraud it could earn.
